newsitem.title: GERMANY: Oil World sees sharply lower EU rapeseed supply.
newsitem.headline: Oil World sees sharply lower EU rapeseed supply.

text.p: Lower production and imports will cut European Union rapeseed supplies to 7.7 million tonnes in 1996/97 (July/June), down 1.8 million from the previous season, the Oil World newsletter said.
The independent publication said crushings in the third quarter of 1996, at 1.73 million tonnes, were down 220,000 tonnes from the same 1995 period, as oil yields had dropped.
Imports in July/Sept 1996 were estimated at 80,000 tonnes against 209,000 last year.
Total imports in the July 96-June 97 season might not exceed 300,000 tonnes, compared with 865,000 in 95/96.
But exports to Poland would pick up as the country needed 200,000 tonnes of imports after winter damage to its 1996 crop.
Total EU 96/97 rapeseed exports to third countries could be 240,000 tonnes versus 118,000 tonnes in 95/96.
But favourable domestic sunseed supplies and Russian and Ukrainian imports may ease the tight rapeseed sitution.
EU 96/97 sunseed output was put at 3.9 million tonnes, up 600,000 from 95/96, mostly due to higher Spanish crops.

EU soybean imports in July-Sept 96 would be down at 3.20 million tonnes (3.72 million 95) and crushings at 3.05 million (3.48) as feed grain prices were becoming more attractive. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
